using ForwardDiff   # explicit gradients for Optim (autodiff kwarg pipeline broken in current Optim)

# PrettyTables v3 compatibility shim. v3 dropped `ft_printf` (now
# `fmt__printf`) and requires the `formatters` keyword to be a Vector.
# All call sites in this document use the v2 form
# `formatters = PrettyTables.ft_printf(fmt, cols)`; re-create
# `ft_printf` so it returns a single-element Vector wrapping the new
# `fmt__printf`, accepting either an Int column index or a range.
if !isdefined(PrettyTables, :ft_printf)
    @eval PrettyTables begin
        ft_printf(fmt, cols) =
            [fmt__printf(fmt, collect(cols isa Integer ? (cols:cols) : cols))]
        ft_printf(fmt) = [fmt__printf(fmt)]   # apply to all columns (v2 single-arg)
    end
end

# PrettyTables v3 also renamed the `header` keyword to `column_labels`
# (which must be an `AbstractVector` — a flat vector for one header row,
# or a vector of row-vectors for stacked headers; a Tuple is rejected).
# `_pt_compat` wraps `pretty_table` so the document's v2-style calls keep
# working: it maps `header` → `column_labels` (Tuple → Vector), and
# normalises `formatters` to a flat Vector. All `PrettyTables.pretty_table`
# call sites in the document route through this wrapper. `_PT_REAL` holds
# the real function (no trailing `(`, so the route-through rewrite leaves
# it untouched — no recursion).
const _PT_REAL = PrettyTables.pretty_table
function _pt_compat(data; header = nothing, formatters = nothing,
                    body_hlines = nothing, kwargs...)
    kw = Dict{Symbol,Any}(kwargs)
    if header !== nothing
        kw[:column_labels] = header isa Tuple ? collect(header) : header
    end
    if formatters !== nothing
        kw[:formatters] =
            formatters isa Function ? [formatters] :
            formatters isa Tuple ?
                collect(Iterators.flatten(
                    x isa Union{AbstractVector,Tuple} ? x : (x,) for x in formatters)) :
                formatters
    end
    # `body_hlines` (v2) has no v3 equivalent — it only drew cosmetic
    # horizontal rules after given rows. Captured here and dropped so the
    # table still renders (without the extra separators). `alignment` and
    # `row_labels` are unchanged in v3 and pass straight through.
    return _PT_REAL(data; kw...)
end

# Optim autodiff compat shim. The installed Optim's `autodiff` kwarg
# rejects the Symbol form `:forward` (it now expects an ADTypes type),
# and even the ADTypes path trips a DifferentiationInterface bug in
# this version. The fix: don't use Optim's autodiff plumbing at all —
# wrap `f` with an explicit ForwardDiff-computed gradient and call the
# 5-arg `optimize(f, g!, x0, method, opts)` form, which doesn't go
# through autodiff. `_optimize_compat` routes every Optim.optimize call
# in the document through this translation; 4-arg calls with
# `autodiff = :forward` are rewritten to the 5-arg gradient form, all
# other shapes pass through. `_OPT_REAL` holds the real function (no
# trailing `(`, so the route-through rewrite leaves it untouched).
const _OPT_REAL = Optim.optimize
function _optimize_compat(args...; kwargs...)
    kw = Dict{Symbol,Any}(kwargs)
    ad = pop!(kw, :autodiff, nothing)
    # If `autodiff = :forward` is requested, build the gradient via
    # ForwardDiff and use the explicit-gradient path. Handles any arg
    # shape where args[1]=f, args[2]=x0 (method/options follow): 3-arg
    # `(f, x0, method)`, 4-arg `(f, x0, method, opts)`, etc.
    if ad isa Symbol && (ad === :forward || ad === :forwarddiff) && length(args) >= 2
        f, x0 = args[1], args[2]
        g!(g, x) = ForwardDiff.gradient!(g, f, x)
        return _OPT_REAL(f, g!, x0, args[3:end]...; kw...)
    end
    return ad === nothing ? _OPT_REAL(args...; kw...) :
                            _OPT_REAL(args...; autodiff = ad, kw...)
end

```{julia}
_rawval(x) = hasproperty(x, :value) ? x.value : x  # unwrap ReadStatTables.LabeledValue

function _numeric_vec(col)
    vals = collect(skipmissing(col))
    isempty(vals) && return Float64[]
    T = Base.nonmissingtype(eltype(col))
    T <: Real && return convert(Vector{Float64}, vals)
    try
        return Float64[Float64(_rawval(v)) for v in vals]
    catch
        return nothing  # non-numeric (strings, etc.)
    end
end

"""
Expand a Stata-style varlist pattern against DataFrame columns. Supports:
  * `t*`, `*t`, `*mpg*`, `t?`   — glob wildcards
  * `price-weight`              — range of columns (inclusive, by column order)
  * exact names, Symbols, vectors, and the literal "_all"
"""
function _expand_varlist(df, vars)
    cols = string.(DataFrames.names(df))
    patterns = vars isa Union{Symbol,AbstractString} ? [string(vars)] :
               vars isa AbstractVector ? [string(v) for v in vars] :
               [string(v) for v in collect(vars)]

    out = String[]
    for p in patterns
        if p == "_all"
            append!(out, cols)
        elseif occursin('*', p) || occursin('?', p)
            rx = Regex("^" * replace(p, "*" => ".*", "?" => ".") * "\$")
            for c in cols
                occursin(rx, c) && push!(out, c)
            end
        elseif occursin('-', p) && !startswith(p, "-") && !(p in cols)
            parts = split(p, '-', limit=2)
            i = findfirst(==(String(parts[1])), cols)
            j = findfirst(==(String(parts[2])), cols)
            (i === nothing || j === nothing) && error("Unknown variable in range '$p'")
            i, j = minmax(i, j)
            append!(out, cols[i:j])
        else
            push!(out, p)
        end
    end

    seen = Set{String}(); uniq = String[]
    for v in out
        v in seen || (push!(seen, v); push!(uniq, v))
    end
    return Symbol.(uniq)
end

function summarize_stata(df::DataFrames.AbstractDataFrame, vars=nothing; detail::Bool=false)
    if vars === nothing
        varlist = Symbol[]
        for n in DataFrames.names(df)
            _numeric_vec(df[!, n]) === nothing || push!(varlist, Symbol(n))
        end
    else
        varlist = _expand_varlist(df, vars)
    end

    rows = []
    for v in varlist
        xraw = _numeric_vec(df[!, v])
        x = xraw === nothing ? Float64[] : xraw
        n = length(x)
        if n == 0
            push!(rows, (; Variable=string(v), Obs=0, Mean=missing,
                           Std=missing, Min=missing, Max=missing))
            continue
        end
        μ  = Statistics.mean(x)
        σ  = n > 1 ? Statistics.std(x) : missing
        base = (; Variable=string(v), Obs=n, Mean=μ, Std=σ,
                  Min=minimum(x), Max=maximum(x))
        if detail
            qs = Statistics.quantile(x, [0.01,0.05,0.10,0.25,0.50,0.75,0.90,0.95,0.99])
            # Stata uses biased moments for skewness/kurtosis
            m2 = Statistics.mean((x .- μ).^2)
            m3 = Statistics.mean((x .- μ).^3)
            m4 = Statistics.mean((x .- μ).^4)
            skew = m2 > 0 ? m3 / m2^(3/2) : missing
            kurt = m2 > 0 ? m4 / m2^2     : missing
            push!(rows, merge(base,
                (; p1=qs[1], p5=qs[2], p10=qs[3], p25=qs[4], p50=qs[5],
                   p75=qs[6], p90=qs[7], p95=qs[8], p99=qs[9],
                   Variance = ismissing(σ) ? missing : σ^2,
                   Skewness = skew, Kurtosis = kurt)))
        else
            push!(rows, base)
        end
    end

    # Stata's `summarize, detail` block — one per requested variable.
    if detail
        _g9d(x; w::Int = 9, mx::Int = 7) = begin
            (ismissing(x) || !isfinite(x)) && return "."
            sig = mx
            s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig, x)
            while length(s) > w && sig > 1
                sig -= 1; s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig, x)
            end
            0 < abs(x) < 1 ? replace(s, r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1.") : s
        end
        _comma_d(n::Integer) = replace(string(n), r"(\d)(?=(\d{3})+$)" => s"\1,")
        for r in rows
            v = r.Variable
            x = _numeric_vec(df[!, Symbol(v)])
            x === nothing && (println("$v: not numeric"); continue)
            n = length(x); ssorted = sort(x)
            small4 = ssorted[1:min(4, n)]
            large4 = ssorted[max(1, n - 3):n]    # ascending; Stata also shows ascending here
            println()
            println(lpad(v, 36))
            println("-"^61)
            println(lpad("Percentiles", 26),  lpad("Smallest", 16))
            pct = [0.01, 0.05, 0.10, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 0.90, 0.95, 0.99]
            qs  = Statistics.quantile(x, pct)
            sml = [get(small4, i, missing) for i in 1:4]
            lrg = [get(large4, i, missing) for i in 1:4]
            # Row 1: 1% / small[1]
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s\n", "1%",
                           _g9d(qs[1]), _g9d(sml[1]))
            # Row 2: 5% / small[2]
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s\n", "5%",
                           _g9d(qs[2]), _g9d(sml[2]))
            # Row 3: 10% / small[3]                Obs <N>
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s%14s %s\n", "10%",
                           _g9d(qs[3]), _g9d(sml[3]),
                           "Obs", _comma_d(n))
            # Row 4: 25% / small[4]                Sum of wgt.
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s%14s %s\n", "25%",
                           _g9d(qs[4]), _g9d(sml[4]),
                           "Sum of wgt.", _comma_d(n))
            println()
            # Row 5: 50% / blank          Mean
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s%14s %s\n", "50%",
                           _g9d(qs[5]), "", "Mean", _g9d(r.Mean))
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s%14s %s\n",
                           "", "", "Largest",
                           "Std. dev.", _g9d(r.Std))
            # Row 6: 75% / large[1]
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s\n", "75%",
                           _g9d(qs[6]), _g9d(lrg[1]))
            println()
            # Row 7: 90% / large[2]                Variance
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s%14s %s\n", "90%",
                           _g9d(qs[7]), _g9d(lrg[2]),
                           "Variance", _g9d(r.Variance))
            # Row 8: 95% / large[3]                Skewness
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s%14s %s\n", "95%",
                           _g9d(qs[8]), _g9d(lrg[3]),
                           "Skewness", _g9d(r.Skewness))
            # Row 9: 99% / large[4]                Kurtosis
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s%14s %s\n", "99%",
                           _g9d(qs[9]), _g9d(lrg[4]),
                           "Kurtosis", _g9d(r.Kurtosis))
        end
        return
    end

    # Stata %9.0g: up to 7 sig figs, capped at 9 chars total (so leading "0."
    # for |x|<1 fits), then leading "0" stripped from |x|<1.
    _g9(x; w::Int=9, mx::Int=7) = begin
        (ismissing(x) || !isfinite(x)) && return "."
        sig = mx
        s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig, x)
        while length(s) > w && sig > 1
            sig -= 1
            s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig, x)
        end
        0 < abs(x) < 1 ? replace(s, r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1.") : s
    end
    _comma(num::Integer) = begin
        s = string(abs(num)); parts = String[]; i = length(s)
        while i >= 1; push!(parts, s[max(1, i-2):i]); i -= 3; end
        (num < 0 ? "-" : "") * join(reverse(parts), ",")
    end

    println("    Variable |        Obs        Mean    Std. dev.       Min        Max")
    println("-"^13, "+", "-"^57)
    for r in rows
        Printf.@printf("%12s |  %9s   %9s   %9s  %9s  %9s\n",
                       r.Variable, _comma(r.Obs),
                       _g9(r.Mean), _g9(r.Std),
                       _g9(r.Min),  _g9(r.Max))
    end
end

"""
    regress_stata(model; level=0.95)

Stata-style `regress` output — prints the ANOVA table, overall F-statistic,
R², adjusted R², Root MSE, and the coefficient table with t-statistics,
p-values, and confidence intervals, matching the format of Stata's
`regress` command. The intercept is relabelled `_cons`.

Works with any `StatsBase`-compatible OLS model, e.g. the output of
`FixedEffectModels.reg(df, @formula(y ~ x2 + x3))`.
"""
function regress_stata(model; level::Float64=0.95, noheader::Bool=false)
    β      = StatsBase.coef(model)
    V      = StatsBase.vcov(model)
    se     = sqrt.(max.(LinearAlgebra.diag(V), 0.0))
    nm_raw = string.(StatsBase.coefnames(model))
    nm     = replace.(nm_raw, "(Intercept)" => "_cons")
    has_int = any(==("_cons"), nm)

    n      = Int(StatsBase.nobs(model))
    rss    = StatsBase.deviance(model)
    r2     = StatsBase.r2(model)
    ar2    = StatsBase.adjr2(model)
    dof_r  = Int(StatsBase.dof_residual(model))
    k      = length(β) - (has_int ? 1 : 0)
    tss    = rss / max(1 - r2, eps())
    mss    = tss - rss
    rmse   = sqrt(rss / dof_r)
    Fstat  = (mss / k) / (rss / dof_r)
    pF     = 1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.FDist(k, dof_r), Fstat)

    yname = try
        string(StatsBase.responsename(model))
    catch
        hasproperty(model, :yname) ? string(model.yname) : "y"
    end

    t_stat = β ./ se
    tcrit  = Distributions.quantile(Distributions.TDist(dof_r), 1 - (1-level)/2)
    p_val  = 2 .* (1 .- Distributions.cdf.(Distributions.TDist(dof_r), abs.(t_stat)))
    ci_lo  = β .- tcrit .* se
    ci_hi  = β .+ tcrit .* se

    # Stata %10.0g-style: `sig` significant digits, strip leading 0 for |x|<1,
    # right-aligned in width `w`.
    function _g(x, w; sig=7)
        (ismissing(x) || !isfinite(x)) && return Printf.@sprintf("%*s", w, ".")
        s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig, x)
        if 0 < abs(x) < 1
            s = replace(s, r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1.")
        end
        return Printf.@sprintf("%*s", w, s)
    end

    # ── ANOVA table + summary-stats block (skipped when `noheader=true`,
    # matching Stata's `regress y x, noheader` option)
    if !noheader
        println()
        Printf.@printf("%12s | %10s %10s %10s    %-13s = %10d\n",
                       "Source", "SS", "df", "MS", "Number of obs", n)
        println("-"^13, "+", "-"^34, "   ",
                Printf.@sprintf("%-13s = %10.2f", "F($k, $dof_r)", Fstat))
        Printf.@printf("%12s | %s %10d %s    %-13s = %10.4f\n",
                       "Model", _g(mss, 10), k, _g(mss/k, 10), "Prob > F", pF)
        Printf.@printf("%12s | %s %10d %s    %-13s = %10.4f\n",
                       "Residual", _g(rss, 10), dof_r, _g(rss/dof_r, 10),
                       "R-squared", r2)
        println("-"^13, "+", "-"^34, "   ",
                Printf.@sprintf("%-13s = %10.4f", "Adj R-squared", ar2))
        Printf.@printf("%12s | %s %10d %s    %-13s = %10.4f\n",
                       "Total", _g(tss, 10), n-1, _g(tss/(n-1), 10),
                       "Root MSE", rmse)
    end
    println()

    # ── Coefficient table
    println("-"^78)
    Printf.@printf("%12s | %10s  %9s  %6s  %5s     [%d%% conf. interval]\n",
                   yname, "Coefficient", "Std. err.", "t", "P>|t|",
                   round(Int, 100*level))
    println("-"^13, "+", "-"^64)
    for i in eachindex(β)
        Printf.@printf("%12s | %s  %s  %6.2f  %5.3f  %s  %s\n",
                       nm[i],
                       _g(β[i], 10),
                       _g(se[i], 9),
                       t_stat[i],
                       p_val[i],
                       _g(ci_lo[i], 11),
                       _g(ci_hi[i], 11))
    end
    println("-"^78)
    return nothing
end

"""
    regress_stata(df, y, xs; level=0.95, vcov=nothing)

Convenience method: fit `y ~ xs…` on `df` with `FixedEffectModels.reg` and
print the Stata-style `regress` output. `y` is the dependent variable (Symbol
or String); `xs` is a Symbol, String, or vector of regressor names. Pass
`vcov=Vcov.robust()` (or similar) for non-default standard errors.

Example:

    regress_stata(df5, :y, [:x2, :x3])
    regress_stata(df5, :y, [:x2, :x3]; vcov=Vcov.robust())
"""
function regress_stata(df::DataFrames.AbstractDataFrame, y, xs;
                       level::Float64=0.95, vcov=nothing, weights=nothing,
                       noheader::Bool=false)
    ys  = Symbol(y)
    xsv = xs isa Union{Symbol,AbstractString} ? [Symbol(xs)] :
          [Symbol(v) for v in xs]
    f = term(ys) ~ sum(term.(xsv))
    kw = weights === nothing ? (;) : (; weights=Symbol(weights))
    m = vcov === nothing ?
        FixedEffectModels.reg(df, f; kw...) :
        FixedEffectModels.reg(df, f, vcov; kw...)
    regress_stata(m; level=level, noheader=noheader)
    return nothing
end

"""
    sureg_fit(df, eqs::Pair...; reps=0, seed=nothing)

Silent companion to `sureg`: runs the same FGLS SUR (with optional bootstrap
vcov) and returns a `NamedTuple` of results — no printing. Use this before
`test_sureg` to run cross-equation Wald tests on the stored fit.

Fields: `β`, `V`, `coefnames` (as `"[eqname]var"`), `eqnames`, `cns`, `ks`,
`offsets`, `N`, `Σ̂`, `β_eq`, `V_eq`, `se_eq`, `rmse`, `r2s`, `chi2s`,
`pvals`, `reps`.
"""
function sureg_fit(df::DataFrames.AbstractDataFrame, eqs::Pair...;
                   reps::Int=0, seed::Union{Int,Nothing}=nothing,
                   constraints::AbstractVector=String[])
    M = length(eqs)
    all_vars = Symbol[]
    for (y, xs) in eqs
        push!(all_vars, Symbol(y))
        xsv = xs isa Union{Symbol,AbstractString} ? [Symbol(xs)] :
              [Symbol(v) for v in xs]
        append!(all_vars, xsv)
    end
    d = DataFrames.dropmissing(df, unique(all_vars))
    N = DataFrames.nrow(d)

    Xs      = Vector{Matrix{Float64}}(undef, M)
    Ys      = Vector{Vector{Float64}}(undef, M)
    cns     = Vector{Vector{String}}(undef, M)
    eqnames = Vector{String}(undef, M)
    for (j, (y, xs)) in enumerate(eqs)
        ys  = Symbol(y)
        xsv = xs isa Union{Symbol,AbstractString} ? [Symbol(xs)] :
              [Symbol(v) for v in xs]
        Xs[j] = hcat(ones(N), [Float64.(_rawval.(d[!, v])) for v in xsv]...)
        Ys[j] = Float64.(_rawval.(d[!, ys]))
        cns[j] = vcat("_cons", string.(xsv))  # intercept at column 1
        eqnames[j] = string(ys)
    end
    ks      = [size(X, 2) for X in Xs]
    kt      = sum(ks)
    offsets = vcat(0, cumsum(ks))

    # Full coefnames used for constraint parsing and reporting.
    coefnames_full = String[]
    for j in 1:M, i in 1:ks[j]
        push!(coefnames_full, "[$(eqnames[j])]$(cns[j][i])")
    end

    # Parse constraint strings into (R, r) — same grammar as `test_sureg`.
    R_con = zeros(0, kt); r_con = Float64[]; con_labels = String[]
    if !isempty(constraints)
        function _resolve(token::AbstractString)
            tok = String(strip(token))
            num = tryparse(Float64, tok)
            num !== nothing && return (Int[], num)
            if startswith(tok, "[") && occursin(']', tok)
                k = findfirst(==(tok), coefnames_full)
                k === nothing && error("Coefficient not found: $tok")
                return ([k], 0.0)
            end
            idx = Int[]
            for (k, cn) in enumerate(coefnames_full)
                m = match(r"^\[(.+)\](.+)$", cn)
                (m === nothing || m.captures[2] != tok) && continue
                push!(idx, k)
            end
            isempty(idx) && error("Coefficient not found in any equation: $tok")
            return (idx, 0.0)
        end
        R_rows = Vector{Vector{Float64}}()
        for c in constraints
            cs = strip(string(c))
            occursin('=', cs) ||
                error("Constraint must contain '=': got '$cs'")
            lhs_s, rhs_s = split(cs, '='; limit=2)
            lhs_idx, lhs_c = _resolve(lhs_s)
            rhs_idx, rhs_c = _resolve(rhs_s)
            (length(lhs_idx) > 1 || length(rhs_idx) > 1) &&
                error("Ambiguous short name in '$cs' — use [eq]name")
            row = zeros(kt)
            for k in lhs_idx; row[k] += 1.0; end
            for k in rhs_idx; row[k] -= 1.0; end
            push!(R_rows, row); push!(r_con, rhs_c - lhs_c)
            push!(con_labels,
                  !isempty(lhs_idx) && !isempty(rhs_idx) ?
                      "$(coefnames_full[lhs_idx[1]]) = $(coefnames_full[rhs_idx[1]])" :
                  !isempty(lhs_idx) ?
                      "$(coefnames_full[lhs_idx[1]]) = $(rhs_c)" :
                      "$(coefnames_full[rhs_idx[1]]) = $(lhs_c)")
        end
        R_con = reduce(vcat, permutedims.(R_rows))
    end
    has_con = !isempty(con_labels)

    # Projection of (β_u, V_u) onto Rβ = r.
    function _constrain(β_u, V_u)
        has_con || return (β_u, V_u)
        RVR   = R_con * V_u * R_con'
        VRT   = V_u * R_con'
        β_c   = β_u .- VRT * (RVR \ (R_con * β_u .- r_con))
        V_c   = V_u .- VRT * LinearAlgebra.inv(RVR) * R_con * V_u
        return (β_c, V_c)
    end

    # Step 1: OLS residuals → Σ̂
    β_ols = [Xs[j] \ Ys[j] for j in 1:M]
    e_ols = [Ys[j] - Xs[j] * β_ols[j] for j in 1:M]
    Σ̂ = [LinearAlgebra.dot(e_ols[i], e_ols[j]) / N for i in 1:M, j in 1:M]

    # Step 2: FGLS via blocked (Σ⁻¹ ⊗ I) sandwich
    Σinv = LinearAlgebra.inv(Σ̂)
    XWX  = zeros(kt, kt)
    XWY  = zeros(kt)
    for i in 1:M, j in 1:M
        ri = (offsets[i]+1):offsets[i+1]
        rj = (offsets[j]+1):offsets[j+1]
        XWX[ri, rj] .= Σinv[i, j] .* (Xs[i]' * Xs[j])
        XWY[ri]    .+= Σinv[i, j] .* (Xs[i]' * Ys[j])
    end
    β_u_full = XWX \ XWY
    V_u_full = LinearAlgebra.inv(XWX)
    β_sur, V_sur = _constrain(β_u_full, V_u_full)

    β_eq  = [β_sur[(offsets[j]+1):offsets[j+1]]                              for j in 1:M]
    V_eq  = [V_sur[(offsets[j]+1):offsets[j+1], (offsets[j]+1):offsets[j+1]] for j in 1:M]
    se_eq = [sqrt.(max.(LinearAlgebra.diag(V), 0.0)) for V in V_eq]
    e_sur = [Ys[j] - Xs[j] * β_eq[j] for j in 1:M]

    rmse  = [sqrt(LinearAlgebra.dot(e_sur[j], e_sur[j]) / N) for j in 1:M]
    r2s   = Float64[]; chi2s = Float64[]; pvals = Float64[]
    for j in 1:M
        rss = LinearAlgebra.dot(e_sur[j], e_sur[j])
        tss = sum((Ys[j] .- Statistics.mean(Ys[j])).^2)
        push!(r2s, 1 - rss / tss)
        slope = 2:ks[j]     # exclude intercept (column 1)
        βs = β_eq[j][slope]; Vs = V_eq[j][slope, slope]
        # pinv handles rank-deficient V_s when constraints bind on this block.
        χ2 = βs' * LinearAlgebra.pinv(Vs) * βs
        push!(chi2s, χ2)
        push!(pvals, 1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Chisq(length(slope)), χ2))
    end

    # ── Bootstrap vcov (replaces V̂_SUR for the coefficient table SEs/CIs;
    #     summary-block χ² is unchanged and still uses the analytical V̂_SUR).
    if reps > 0
        seed !== nothing && Random.seed!(seed)
        β_boot = Matrix{Float64}(undef, reps, kt)
        for b in 1:reps
            idx  = StatsBase.sample(1:N, N; replace=true)
            Xs_b = [X[idx, :]   for X in Xs]
            Ys_b = [Y[idx]      for Y in Ys]
            β_ols_b = [Xs_b[j] \ Ys_b[j] for j in 1:M]
            e_b     = [Ys_b[j] - Xs_b[j] * β_ols_b[j] for j in 1:M]
            Σ_b     = [LinearAlgebra.dot(e_b[i], e_b[j]) / N for i in 1:M, j in 1:M]
            Σinv_b  = LinearAlgebra.inv(Σ_b)
            XWX_b = zeros(kt, kt); XWY_b = zeros(kt)
            for i in 1:M, j in 1:M
                ri = (offsets[i]+1):offsets[i+1]
                rj = (offsets[j]+1):offsets[j+1]
                XWX_b[ri, rj] .= Σinv_b[i, j] .* (Xs_b[i]' * Xs_b[j])
                XWY_b[ri]    .+= Σinv_b[i, j] .* (Xs_b[i]' * Ys_b[j])
            end
            β_ub = XWX_b \ XWY_b
            if has_con
                V_ub = LinearAlgebra.inv(XWX_b)
                β_ub, _ = _constrain(β_ub, V_ub)
            end
            β_boot[b, :] = β_ub
        end
        V_sur = Statistics.cov(β_boot)
        V_eq  = [V_sur[(offsets[j]+1):offsets[j+1], (offsets[j]+1):offsets[j+1]] for j in 1:M]
        se_eq = [sqrt.(max.(LinearAlgebra.diag(V), 0.0)) for V in V_eq]
    end

    return (; β=β_sur, V=V_sur, coefnames=coefnames_full,
              eqnames, cns, ks, offsets, N, Σ̂,
              β_eq, V_eq, se_eq,
              rmse, r2s, chi2s, pvals, reps,
              constraints=con_labels)
end

"""
    sureg(df, (y1 => [x1s…]), (y2 => [x2s…]), …;
          level=0.95, reps=0, seed=nothing)

Stata-style `sureg` — seemingly unrelated regression (FGLS). Each pair
`y => xs` becomes an equation `y ~ 1 + xs…`. Prints Stata's `sureg` summary
block (Obs, Params, RMSE, R², χ², P>χ²), the pooled coefficient table with
z-statistics, the residual correlation matrix, and the Breusch–Pagan test
of independence against a diagonal Σ.

Algorithm: equation-by-equation OLS gives Σ̂ = (eᵢ′eⱼ)/N; a single FGLS
step with W = Σ̂⁻¹ ⊗ Iₙ recovers β̂_SUR and V̂_SUR. The correlation matrix
and BP test use the OLS-step Σ̂ (matching Stata's default non-iterated
`sureg`).

Pass `reps=400, seed=10101` to mimic Stata's `bootstrap, reps(400) seed(10101): sureg …` —
β̂_SUR is kept as the observed coefficient, but V̂_SUR is replaced by the
sample covariance of B bootstrap replications (each a full SUR on a
resampled dataset). The coefficient table header changes to
"Observed coefficient | Bootstrap std. err. | Normal-based CI". The summary
block's χ² still uses the analytical V̂_SUR to match Stata.

Examples:

    sureg(df_sur,
          :ldrugexp => [:age, :age2, :actlim, :totchr, :medicaid, :private],
          :ltotothr => [:age, :age2, :educyr, :actlim, :totchr, :private])

    sureg(df_sur,
          :ldrugexp => [:age, :age2, :actlim, :totchr, :medicaid, :private],
          :ltotothr => [:age, :age2, :educyr, :actlim, :totchr, :private];
          reps=400, seed=10101)
"""
function sureg(df::DataFrames.AbstractDataFrame, eqs::Pair...;
               level::Float64=0.95, reps::Int=0,
               seed::Union{Int,Nothing}=nothing,
               constraints::AbstractVector=String[])
    fit = sureg_fit(df, eqs...; reps=reps, seed=seed, constraints=constraints)
    if !isempty(fit.constraints)
        println("Constraints imposed:")
        for (i, c) in enumerate(fit.constraints)
            Printf.@printf(" ( %d)  %s\n", i, c)
        end
        println()
    end
    M       = length(fit.eqnames)
    eqnames = fit.eqnames
    cns     = fit.cns
    ks      = fit.ks
    N       = fit.N
    β_eq    = fit.β_eq
    se_eq   = fit.se_eq
    rmse    = fit.rmse
    r2s     = fit.r2s
    chi2s   = fit.chi2s
    pvals   = fit.pvals
    Σ̂       = fit.Σ̂

    # ── Summary table (PrettyTables)
    println("Seemingly unrelated regression\n")
    summary_df = DataFrames.DataFrame(
        Equation    = eqnames,
        Obs         = fill(N, M),
        Params      = [k - 1 for k in ks],
        RMSE        = rmse,
        R_squared   = r2s,
        chi2        = chi2s,
        P_chi2      = pvals,
    )
    _pt_compat(summary_df;
        header     = ["Equation", "Obs", "Params", "RMSE", "R-squared",
                      "chi2", "P>chi2"],
        formatters = vcat(
            PrettyTables.ft_printf("%.6f", [4]),
            PrettyTables.ft_printf("%.4f", [5, 7]),
            PrettyTables.ft_printf("%.2f", [6]),
        ),
        alignment  = [:l, :r, :r, :r, :r, :r, :r],
    )

    # ── Coefficient table (PrettyTables), slopes first then intercept
    zcrit = Distributions.quantile(Distributions.Normal(), 1 - (1-level)/2)
    eqn_col  = String[]; var_col = String[]
    β_col    = Float64[]; se_col  = Float64[]
    z_col    = Float64[]; p_col   = Float64[]
    lo_col   = Float64[]; hi_col  = Float64[]
    hline_at = Int[]
    nrows    = 0
    for j in 1:M
        order = vcat(collect(2:ks[j]), 1)
        first_row = true
        for i in order
            β_i  = β_eq[j][i]
            se_i = se_eq[j][i]
            z_i  = β_i / se_i
            p_i  = 2 * (1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Normal(), abs(z_i)))
            push!(eqn_col, first_row ? eqnames[j] : "")
            push!(var_col, cns[j][i])
            push!(β_col, β_i);   push!(se_col, se_i)
            push!(z_col, z_i);   push!(p_col, p_i)
            push!(lo_col, β_i - zcrit * se_i)
            push!(hi_col, β_i + zcrit * se_i)
            first_row = false
            nrows += 1
        end
        j < M && push!(hline_at, nrows)
    end
    coef_df = DataFrames.DataFrame(
        Equation     = eqn_col,
        Variable     = var_col,
        Coefficient  = β_col,
        StdErr       = se_col,
        z            = z_col,
        p            = p_col,
        CI_low       = lo_col,
        CI_high      = hi_col,
    )
    lvl = round(Int, 100 * level)
    println()
    coef_header = reps > 0 ?
        (["", "", "Observed", "Bootstrap", "", "", "Normal-based", ""],
         ["Equation", "Variable", "coefficient", "std. err.",
          "z", "P>|z|", "[$(lvl)% CI low]", "[$(lvl)% CI high]"]) :
        ["Equation", "Variable", "Coefficient", "Std. err.",
         "z", "P>|z|", "[$(lvl)% CI low]", "[$(lvl)% CI high]"]
    _pt_compat(coef_df;
        header     = coef_header,
        formatters = vcat(
            PrettyTables.ft_printf("%.7f", [3, 4, 7, 8]),
            PrettyTables.ft_printf("%.2f",  [5]),
            PrettyTables.ft_printf("%.3f",  [6]),
        ),
        body_hlines = hline_at,
        alignment   = [:l, :l, :r, :r, :r, :r, :r, :r],
    )
    reps > 0 && Printf.@printf("  (bootstrap replications = %d)\n", reps)

    # ── Residual correlation matrix (from OLS-step Σ̂)
    Rmat = [Σ̂[i, j] / sqrt(Σ̂[i, i] * Σ̂[j, j]) for i in 1:M, j in 1:M]
    corr_strs = [j <= i ? Printf.@sprintf("%.4f", Rmat[i, j]) : ""
                 for i in 1:M, j in 1:M]
    println("\nCorrelation matrix of residuals:\n")
    _pt_compat(corr_strs;
        header     = eqnames,
        row_labels = eqnames,
        alignment  = fill(:r, M),
    )

    # ── Breusch–Pagan test of independence
    bp = 0.0
    for i in 1:M-1, j in (i+1):M
        bp += Rmat[i, j]^2
    end
    bp *= N
    df_bp = M * (M - 1) ÷ 2
    p_bp  = 1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Chisq(df_bp), bp)
    Printf.@printf("\nBreusch–Pagan test of independence: chi2(%d) = %.3f, Pr = %.4f\n",
                   df_bp, bp, p_bp)
    return nothing
end

"""
    test_sureg(fit, vars)

Stata-style `test <varlist>` after `sureg`/`sureg_fit`. Jointly tests that
every coefficient whose short name matches any of `vars` is zero **in every
equation where it appears** — exactly what Stata's `test age age2` does
after `sureg`. Uses the stored joint vcov from `fit`, so cross-equation
covariances are respected (and the bootstrap vcov is used if the fit was
made with `reps>0`).

Output mirrors Stata's:

    ( 1)  [eq1]v1 = 0
    ( 2)  [eq2]v1 = 0
    ...
            chi2(q) =   W
          Prob > chi2 =  p

Example:

    fit = sureg_fit(df_sur,
                    :ldrugexp => [:age, :age2, :actlim, :totchr, :medicaid, :private],
                    :ltotothr => [:age, :age2, :educyr, :actlim, :totchr, :private])
    test_sureg(fit, [:age, :age2])
"""
function test_sureg(fit, vars::AbstractVector;
                    df_F::Union{Integer,Nothing}=nothing)
    coefnames = fit.coefnames
    K         = length(coefnames)

    # Resolve a single token to either (idx=Int[], number) or
    # (coef_idx_list, 0.0). Short names may match >1 equation; `[eq]var` must
    # match exactly one.
    function _resolve(token::AbstractString)
        tok = String(strip(token))
        num = tryparse(Float64, tok)
        num !== nothing && return (Int[], num)
        if startswith(tok, "[") && occursin(']', tok)
            k = findfirst(==(tok), coefnames)
            k === nothing && error("Coefficient not found: $tok")
            return ([k], 0.0)
        end
        idx = Int[]
        for (k, cn) in enumerate(coefnames)
            m = match(r"^\[(.+)\](.+)$", cn)
            (m === nothing || m.captures[2] != tok) && continue
            push!(idx, k)
        end
        isempty(idx) && error("Coefficient not found in any equation: $tok")
        return (idx, 0.0)
    end

    R_rows = Vector{Vector{Float64}}()
    r_vals = Float64[]
    labels = String[]

    for v in vars
        vs = strip(string(v))
        if occursin('=', vs)
            # Equality restriction → one row.
            lhs_s, rhs_s = split(vs, '='; limit=2)
            lhs_idx, lhs_c = _resolve(lhs_s)
            rhs_idx, rhs_c = _resolve(rhs_s)
            length(lhs_idx) > 1 &&
                error("Ambiguous short name on lhs of '$vs' — use [eq]name")
            length(rhs_idx) > 1 &&
                error("Ambiguous short name on rhs of '$vs' — use [eq]name")
            row = zeros(K)
            for k in lhs_idx; row[k] += 1.0; end
            for k in rhs_idx; row[k] -= 1.0; end
            push!(R_rows, row)
            push!(r_vals, rhs_c - lhs_c)
            if !isempty(lhs_idx) && !isempty(rhs_idx)
                push!(labels,
                      "$(coefnames[lhs_idx[1]]) - $(coefnames[rhs_idx[1]]) = 0")
            elseif !isempty(lhs_idx)
                push!(labels, "$(coefnames[lhs_idx[1]]) = $(rhs_c)")
            else
                push!(labels, "$(coefnames[rhs_idx[1]]) = $(lhs_c)")
            end
        else
            # Bare token → one zero-restriction per matching coef.
            idx_all, _ = _resolve(vs)
            for k in idx_all
                row = zeros(K); row[k] = 1.0
                push!(R_rows, row)
                push!(r_vals, 0.0)
                push!(labels, "$(coefnames[k]) = 0")
            end
        end
    end
    isempty(R_rows) && error("No restrictions parsed from: $(vars)")

    R = reduce(vcat, permutedims.(R_rows))          # q × K
    r = r_vals
    d = R * fit.β .- r
    W = d' * LinearAlgebra.inv(R * fit.V * R') * d
    q = length(r)

    for (i, lbl) in enumerate(labels)
        Printf.@printf(" ( %d)  %s\n", i, lbl)
    end
    println()

    # F-form if df_F supplied (e.g. after `sqreg_stata`), else χ².
    if df_F === nothing
        p_chi = 1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Chisq(q), W)
        Printf.@printf("           chi2(%3d) = %7.2f\n", q, W)
        Printf.@printf("         Prob > chi2 = %7.4f\n", p_chi)
        return (; chi2=W, df=q, p=p_chi, restrictions=labels, R, r)
    else
        Fs  = W / q
        p_F = 1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.FDist(q, df_F), Fs)
        Printf.@printf("       F(%3d, %5d) = %7.2f\n", q, df_F, Fs)
        Printf.@printf("            Prob > F = %7.4f\n", p_F)
        return (; F=Fs, df1=q, df2=df_F, p=p_F,
                  chi2=W, restrictions=labels, R, r)
    end
end

"""
    qreg_stata(df, y, xs; τ=0.5, level=0.95)

Stata-style `qreg y xs…[, quantile(τ)]` — quantile regression by
minimizing the asymmetric "check" loss
`ρ_τ(u) = u · (τ − 1{u < 0})`. Slopes are listed first in the coefficient
table and `_cons` is last, matching Stata's display order.

Standard errors use the classical **iid** Koenker-Bassett formula
`V̂ = s(τ)² · (X'X)⁻¹`, with sparsity `ω = (û_{τ+h} − û_{τ−h})/(2h)` and
Hall-Sheather bandwidth `h = n^{-1/3} · z_{α/2}^{2/3} ·
(1.5φ(Φ⁻¹(τ))²/(2Φ⁻¹(τ)²+1))^{1/3}`. `s(τ) = √(τ(1−τ)) · ω`. Inference
is t-based on `n − k` df.

Pseudo R² (Koenker–Machado): `1 − MSD/RSD`, where MSD is the minimized
check-loss and RSD is the check-loss of the constant-only model (its
fit is the τ-th quantile of y).
"""
function qreg_stata(df, y, xs::AbstractVector; τ::Float64=0.5,
                    level::Float64=0.95,
                    max_iter::Int=5000, tol::Float64=1e-12,
                    quiet::Bool=false)
    ys   = Symbol(y)
    xsv  = [Symbol(v) for v in xs]
    d    = DataFrames.dropmissing(df, unique(vcat(ys, xsv)))
    n    = DataFrames.nrow(d)
    Y    = Float64.(_rawval.(d[!, ys]))
    Xmat = hcat([Float64.(_rawval.(d[!, v])) for v in xsv]..., ones(n))  # slopes, _cons
    k    = size(Xmat, 2)

    # ── IRLS (majorize-minimize on |u|) — robust for the non-smooth check loss.
    # Majorization: |u| ≤ u²/(2|u*|) + |u*|/2; minimizing the upper bound on
    # Σ ρ_τ(eᵢ) yields  β̂ = (X'WX)⁻¹ [X'W y + (2τ−1) · X'1],  with
    # weights wᵢ = 1/max(|eᵢ*|, δ).  δ is shrunk as iterations progress.
    β   = Xmat \ Y
    one = ones(n)
    δ   = 1e-2
    for iter in 1:max_iter
        e    = Y .- Xmat * β
        δ    = max(min(δ, 0.5 * Statistics.median(abs.(e)) + 1e-12), 1e-10)
        w    = 1.0 ./ max.(abs.(e), δ)
        rhs  = Xmat' * (w .* Y) .+ (2τ - 1) .* (Xmat' * one)
        XtWX = Xmat' * (w .* Xmat)
        β_nw = XtWX \ rhs
        dif  = sqrt(sum((β_nw .- β).^2)) / max(1.0, sqrt(sum(β.^2)))
        β    = β_nw
        dif < tol && break
    end
    û  = Y .- Xmat * β

    _rho(u, τ) = u >= 0 ? τ * u : (τ - 1) * u
    MSD   = sum(_rho(û[i], τ) for i in 1:n)
    q_y   = Statistics.quantile(Y, τ)
    RSD   = sum(_rho(Y[i] - q_y, τ) for i in 1:n)
    R²_ps = 1 - MSD / RSD

    # Hall-Sheather bandwidth and Koenker–Bassett (iid) sparsity
    α     = 1 - level
    z_α   = Distributions.quantile(Distributions.Normal(), 1 - α/2)
    Φinv  = Distributions.quantile(Distributions.Normal(), τ)
    φ_τ   = Distributions.pdf(Distributions.Normal(), Φinv)
    h     = n^(-1/3) * z_α^(2/3) *
            ((1.5 * φ_τ^2) / (2 * Φinv^2 + 1))^(1/3)
    p_up  = min(τ + h, 1 - 1/n)
    p_dn  = max(τ - h, 1/n)
    ω     = (Statistics.quantile(û, p_up) -
             Statistics.quantile(û, p_dn)) / (p_up - p_dn)
    s_τ   = sqrt(τ * (1 - τ)) * ω

    V     = s_τ^2 .* LinearAlgebra.inv(Xmat' * Xmat)
    se    = sqrt.(max.(LinearAlgebra.diag(V), 0.0))

    dofv  = n - k
    t_st  = β ./ se
    tcrit = Distributions.quantile(Distributions.TDist(dofv), 1 - α/2)
    pvals = 2 .* (1 .- Distributions.cdf.(Distributions.TDist(dofv), abs.(t_st)))
    ci_lo = β .- tcrit .* se
    ci_hi = β .+ tcrit .* se

    nms  = vcat(string.(xsv), "_cons")
    if !quiet
        _fmtn(x) = replace(string(x), r"(\d)(?=(\d{3})+$)" => s"\1,")
        title = τ == 0.5 ? "Median regression" :
                            Printf.@sprintf("Quantile regression (τ = %.2f)", τ)
        println()
        header_tail = Printf.@sprintf("Number of obs = %10s", _fmtn(n))
        println(title, " "^max(0, 52 - length(title)), header_tail)
        Printf.@printf("  Raw sum of deviations %.2f (about %g)\n", RSD, q_y)
        left3 = Printf.@sprintf("  Min sum of deviations %.3f", MSD)
        tail3 = Printf.@sprintf("Pseudo R2     = %10.4f", R²_ps)
        println(left3, " "^max(0, 52 - length(left3)), tail3)
        println()

        lvl  = round(Int, 100 * level)
        coef_df = DataFrames.DataFrame(
            Variable    = nms,
            Coefficient = β,
            StdErr      = se,
            t           = t_st,
            p           = pvals,
            CI_low      = ci_lo,
            CI_high     = ci_hi,
        )
        _pt_compat(coef_df;
            header = [string(ys), "Coefficient", "Std. err.",
                      "t", "P>|t|", "[$(lvl)% CI low]", "[$(lvl)% CI high]"],
            formatters = vcat(
                PrettyTables.ft_printf("%.7f", [2, 3, 6, 7]),
                PrettyTables.ft_printf("%.2f",  [4]),
                PrettyTables.ft_printf("%.3f",  [5]),
            ),
            alignment = [:l, :r, :r, :r, :r, :r, :r],
        )
    end

    return (; β, V, se, t=t_st, p=pvals, ci_lo, ci_hi,
              coefnames=nms, n, MSD, RSD, pseudo_R2=R²_ps, τ)
end

"""
    sqreg_stata(df, y, xs; τs=[0.25, 0.5, 0.75], reps=400,
                seed=nothing, level=0.95)

Stata-style `sqreg y xs…, q(τ₁ τ₂ …) reps(B)` — **simultaneous** quantile
regression at several τ values with **bootstrap** standard errors. Each
bootstrap replicate resamples rows once and re-fits every quantile on
the same sample, so covariance across quantiles is preserved (this is
what distinguishes `sqreg` from running `bsqreg` separately at each τ).

Prints the Stata header (`Number of obs`, a line per quantile with its
Pseudo R²) followed by a grouped coefficient table — one block per
quantile — with Bootstrap std. err. and t-based CIs on `n − k` df.
"""
function sqreg_stata(df, y, xs::AbstractVector;
                     τs::AbstractVector{<:Real}=[0.25, 0.50, 0.75],
                     reps::Int=400, seed::Union{Int,Nothing}=nothing,
                     level::Float64=0.95)
    ys  = Symbol(y)
    xsv = [Symbol(v) for v in xs]
    d   = DataFrames.dropmissing(df, unique(vcat(ys, xsv)))
    n   = DataFrames.nrow(d)
    k   = length(xsv) + 1
    Q   = length(τs)

    # Point estimates at each τ (silent).
    fits = [qreg_stata(d, ys, xsv; τ=Float64(τ), quiet=true) for τ in τs]
    β0   = [f.β for f in fits]

    # Paired bootstrap — resample rows once per rep, refit every τ.
    seed !== nothing && Random.seed!(seed)
    β_boot = [Matrix{Float64}(undef, reps, k) for _ in 1:Q]
    for b in 1:reps
        idx = StatsBase.sample(1:n, n; replace=true)
        db  = d[idx, :]
        for (j, τ) in enumerate(τs)
            β_boot[j][b, :] = qreg_stata(db, ys, xsv; τ=Float64(τ), quiet=true).β
        end
    end
    se = [vec(Statistics.std(β_boot[j]; dims=1)) for j in 1:Q]

    # Inference (t on n − k df)
    α     = 1 - level
    dofv  = n - k
    tcrit = Distributions.quantile(Distributions.TDist(dofv), 1 - α/2)
    t_q   = [β0[j] ./ se[j] for j in 1:Q]
    p_q   = [2 .* (1 .- Distributions.cdf.(Distributions.TDist(dofv), abs.(t_q[j])))
             for j in 1:Q]
    lo_q  = [β0[j] .- tcrit .* se[j] for j in 1:Q]
    hi_q  = [β0[j] .+ tcrit .* se[j] for j in 1:Q]

    _fmtn(x) = replace(string(x), r"(\d)(?=(\d{3})+$)" => s"\1,")
    nms  = vcat(string.(xsv), "_cons")

    # ─── Header block
    println()
    title = "Simultaneous quantile regression"
    Printf.@printf("%s%*sNumber of obs = %10s\n",
                   title, max(0, 52 - length(title)), "", _fmtn(n))
    left_boot = Printf.@sprintf("  bootstrap(%d) SEs", reps)
    Printf.@printf("%s%*s.%02d Pseudo R2 = %10.4f\n",
                   left_boot, max(0, 52 - length(left_boot)), "",
                   round(Int, 100*τs[1]), fits[1].pseudo_R2)
    for j in 2:Q
        Printf.@printf("%52s.%02d Pseudo R2 = %10.4f\n",
                       "", round(Int, 100*τs[j]), fits[j].pseudo_R2)
    end
    println()

    # ─── Grouped coefficient table in Stata's exact 78-col layout
    _g(x, w; sig=7) = begin
        (ismissing(x) || !isfinite(x)) && return Printf.@sprintf("%*s", w, ".")
        s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig, x)
        0 < abs(x) < 1 && (s = replace(s, r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1."))
        Printf.@sprintf("%*s", w, s)
    end
    lvl = round(Int, 100 * level)
    println("-"^78)
    Printf.@printf("%12s | %22s\n", "", "Bootstrap")
    Printf.@printf("%12s | %10s  %9s  %6s  %5s     [%d%% conf. interval]\n",
                   string(ys), "Coefficient", "std. err.", "t", "P>|t|", lvl)
    println("-"^13, "+", "-"^64)
    for j in 1:Q
        qlabel = Printf.@sprintf("q%02d", round(Int, 100*τs[j]))
        Printf.@printf("%-12s |\n", qlabel)
        for i in 1:k
            Printf.@printf("%12s | %s  %s  %7.2f  %6.3f  %s  %s\n",
                           nms[i],
                           _g(β0[j][i], 10),
                           _g(se[j][i], 9),
                           t_q[j][i], p_q[j][i],
                           _g(lo_q[j][i], 11),
                           _g(hi_q[j][i], 10))
        end
        j < Q && println("-"^13, "+", "-"^64)
    end
    println("-"^78)

    # Joint (stacked) β, V, coefnames in `[qXX]var` format — enables
    # post-estimation tests across quantiles via `test_sureg`.
    β_joint = reduce(vcat, β0)
    boot_stack = reduce(hcat, β_boot)              # B × (Q·k)
    V_joint = Statistics.cov(boot_stack)
    coefnames_joint = String[]
    for τ in τs, v in nms
        push!(coefnames_joint,
              "[" * Printf.@sprintf("q%02d", round(Int, 100*τ)) * "]" * v)
    end

    return (; β = β_joint, V = V_joint, coefnames = coefnames_joint,
              β_by_q = β0, se, t = t_q, p = p_q,
              ci_lo = lo_q, ci_hi = hi_q,
              pseudo_R2 = [f.pseudo_R2 for f in fits],
              varnames = nms, τs, n, reps, df_resid = dofv)
end

"""
    svy_mean(df, var; stratum, psu, weight, level=0.95)

Stata-style `svy: mean <var>` — Horvitz–Thompson weighted mean of a single
variable with Taylor-linearized standard errors under a stratified single-
stage cluster design. Prints the Stata summary header (Number of strata,
PSUs, obs, Population size, Design df) followed by a `PrettyTables` block
with Mean / Linearized std. err. / confidence interval.

Variance formula: Var(ȳ) ≈ V̂(Σᵢ zᵢ) with zᵢ = wᵢ(yᵢ − ȳ)/Σwᵢ; for each
stratum `h` with `nₕ` PSUs, `V̂ = Σₕ (nₕ/(nₕ−1)) Σⱼ (uₕⱼ − ūₕ)²` where
`uₕⱼ = Σᵢ∈PSUⱼ zᵢ`. Equivalent to Stata's default `svyset ..., ` (with-
replacement PSU sampling, so no FPC is applied). Degrees of freedom =
`#PSUs − #strata`, used for the t-based CI.

Example:

    svy_mean(df_nh, :hgb; stratum=:strata, psu=:psu, weight=:finalwgt)
"""
function svy_mean(df, var; stratum::Symbol, psu::Symbol, weight::Symbol,
                  level::Float64=0.95)
    d = DataFrames.dropmissing(df, [Symbol(var), stratum, psu, weight])
    y = Float64.(_rawval.(d[!, Symbol(var)]))
    w = Float64.(_rawval.(d[!, weight]))
    h = _rawval.(d[!, stratum])
    c = _rawval.(d[!, psu])

    n    = length(y)
    W    = sum(w)
    ybar = sum(w .* y) / W
    z    = w .* (y .- ybar) ./ W               # Taylor-linearized score

    V = 0.0
    strata  = unique(h)
    n_psu   = 0
    for hv in strata
        in_h   = h .== hv
        psus_h = c[in_h]
        z_h    = z[in_h]
        ups    = unique(psus_h)
        nh     = length(ups)
        n_psu += nh
        nh < 2 && continue
        u = [sum(z_h[psus_h .== p]) for p in ups]
        ū = Statistics.mean(u)
        V += (nh / (nh - 1)) * sum((u .- ū).^2)
    end
    se    = sqrt(V)
    n_str = length(strata)
    dfree = n_psu - n_str
    tcrit = Distributions.quantile(Distributions.TDist(dfree), 1 - (1-level)/2)
    ci_lo = ybar - tcrit * se
    ci_hi = ybar + tcrit * se

    _fmtn(x) = replace(string(x), r"(\d)(?=(\d{3})+$)" => s"\1,")

    println("Survey: Mean estimation\n")
    Printf.@printf("Number of strata = %-13d Number of obs   = %11s\n",
                   n_str, _fmtn(n))
    Printf.@printf("Number of PSUs   = %-13d Population size = %11s\n",
                   n_psu, _fmtn(Int(round(W))))
    Printf.@printf("%33s Design df       = %11d\n", "", dfree)
    println()

    lvl = round(Int, 100 * level)
    result = DataFrames.DataFrame(
        Variable = [string(var)],
        Mean     = [ybar],
        StdErr   = [se],
        CI_low   = [ci_lo],
        CI_high  = [ci_hi],
    )
    _pt_compat(result;
        header     = (["",         "",     "Linearized", "",                "" ],
                      ["Variable", "Mean", "std. err.",
                       "[$(lvl)% CI low]", "[$(lvl)% CI high]"]),
        formatters = PrettyTables.ft_printf("%.5f", 2:5),
        alignment  = [:l, :r, :r, :r, :r],
    )
    return (; mean=ybar, se=se, ci=(ci_lo, ci_hi), df=dfree,
              n_obs=n, n_strata=n_str, n_psu, popsize=W)
end

"""
    mean_stata(df, var; level=0.95)

Stata-style `mean <var>` — plain sample mean with SE = `s/√n` and a
t-based CI on df = n − 1. No weights, no clustering. Prints the compact
Stata "Mean estimation" header and a `PrettyTables` block with
Mean / Std. err. / CI.

Example:

    mean_stata(df_nh, :hgb)
"""
function mean_stata(df, var; level::Float64=0.95)
    vs = Symbol(var)
    d  = DataFrames.dropmissing(df, [vs])
    y  = Float64.(_rawval.(d[!, vs]))
    n  = length(y)
    μ  = Statistics.mean(y)
    s  = Statistics.std(y)           # sample std, ddof = 1
    se = s / sqrt(n)
    dfree = n - 1
    tcrit = Distributions.quantile(Distributions.TDist(dfree), 1 - (1-level)/2)
    ci_lo = μ - tcrit * se
    ci_hi = μ + tcrit * se

    _fmtn(x) = replace(string(x), r"(\d)(?=(\d{3})+$)" => s"\1,")
    Printf.@printf("Mean estimation                          Number of obs = %s\n\n",
                   _fmtn(n))

    lvl = round(Int, 100 * level)
    result = DataFrames.DataFrame(
        Variable = [string(var)],
        Mean     = [μ],
        StdErr   = [se],
        CI_low   = [ci_lo],
        CI_high  = [ci_hi],
    )
    _pt_compat(result;
        header     = ["Variable", "Mean", "Std. err.",
                      "[$(lvl)% CI low]", "[$(lvl)% CI high]"],
        formatters = PrettyTables.ft_printf("%.5f", 2:5),
        alignment  = [:l, :r, :r, :r, :r],
    )
    return (; mean=μ, se=se, ci=(ci_lo, ci_hi), df=dfree, n_obs=n)
end

"""
    svy_regress(df, y, xs; stratum, psu, weight, level=0.95)

Stata-style `svy: regress <y> <xs…>` — weighted OLS with Taylor-linearized
(Horvitz–Thompson) cluster-robust standard errors under a stratified
single-stage cluster design. Prints the Stata header block (strata, PSUs,
obs, popsize, design df, model F, Prob > F, R²) followed by a
`PrettyTables` coefficient table with slopes first and `_cons` last.

Variance: `V̂(β̂) = A⁻¹ · V̂(Σ uᵢ) · A⁻¹` where `A = X'WX`, scores
`uᵢ = wᵢ xᵢ eᵢ`, and `V̂(Σ uᵢ) = Σₕ nₕ/(nₕ−1) · Σⱼ (Sₕⱼ − S̄ₕ)(Sₕⱼ − S̄ₕ)'`
with `Sₕⱼ = Σᵢ∈PSUⱼ uᵢ`. Degrees of freedom = #PSUs − #strata. The model
F uses Stata's first-order-corrected denominator df `= design_df − q + 1`.

Example:

    svy_regress(df_nh, :hgb, [:age, :female];
                stratum=:strata, psu=:psu, weight=:finalwgt)
"""
function svy_regress(df, y, xs::AbstractVector; stratum::Symbol, psu::Symbol,
                     weight::Symbol, level::Float64=0.95)
    ys   = Symbol(y)
    xsv  = [Symbol(v) for v in xs]
    d    = DataFrames.dropmissing(df, unique([ys, xsv..., stratum, psu, weight]))
    Y    = Float64.(_rawval.(d[!, ys]))
    w    = Float64.(_rawval.(d[!, weight]))
    h    = _rawval.(d[!, stratum])
    c    = _rawval.(d[!, psu])
    Xcols = [Float64.(_rawval.(d[!, v])) for v in xsv]
    X    = hcat(ones(length(Y)), Xcols...)
    cn   = vcat("_cons", string.(xsv))   # index 1 is intercept

    n    = length(Y)
    k    = size(X, 2)
    q    = k - 1                         # slopes (exclude intercept)

    # β̂ from weighted LS
    XW   = X .* w
    A    = XW' * X
    β    = A \ (XW' * Y)
    e    = Y .- X * β
    U    = XW .* e                       # n × k  (uᵢ = wᵢ xᵢ eᵢ)

    # Cluster/stratum aggregation
    strata = unique(h)
    V_meat = zeros(k, k)
    n_psu  = 0
    for hv in strata
        in_h = h .== hv
        psus = c[in_h]
        U_h  = U[in_h, :]
        ups  = unique(psus)
        nh   = length(ups)
        n_psu += nh
        nh < 2 && continue
        S = reduce(vcat, [sum(U_h[psus .== p, :]; dims=1) for p in ups])  # nh × k
        S̄ = Statistics.mean(S; dims=1)
        centered = S .- S̄
        V_meat .+= (nh / (nh - 1)) .* (centered' * centered)
    end
    A_inv = LinearAlgebra.inv(A)
    V     = A_inv * V_meat * A_inv
    se    = sqrt.(max.(LinearAlgebra.diag(V), 0.0))

    n_str = length(strata)
    dfree = n_psu - n_str

    t_stat = β ./ se
    tcrit  = Distributions.quantile(Distributions.TDist(dfree), 1 - (1-level)/2)
    pvals  = 2 .* (1 .- Distributions.cdf.(Distributions.TDist(dfree), abs.(t_stat)))
    ci_lo  = β .- tcrit .* se
    ci_hi  = β .+ tcrit .* se

    # Model F (slopes = 0), first-order corrected df
    slope  = 2:k
    Wstat  = β[slope]' * (V[slope, slope] \ β[slope])
    Fstat  = Wstat / q
    df2    = dfree - q + 1
    pF     = 1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.FDist(q, df2), Fstat)

    # Weighted R²
    ybar_w = sum(w .* Y) / sum(w)
    rss_w  = sum(w .* e.^2)
    tss_w  = sum(w .* (Y .- ybar_w).^2)
    r2     = 1 - rss_w / tss_w
    W_tot  = sum(w)

    _fmtn(x) = replace(string(x), r"(\d)(?=(\d{3})+$)" => s"\1,")

    println("Survey: Linear regression\n")
    Printf.@printf("Number of strata = %-30dNumber of obs   = %11s\n",
                   n_str, _fmtn(n))
    Printf.@printf("Number of PSUs   = %-30dPopulation size = %11s\n",
                   n_psu, _fmtn(Int(round(W_tot))))
    Printf.@printf("%-49sDesign df       = %11d\n", "", dfree)
    Printf.@printf("%-49s%-16s= %11.2f\n", "", "F($q, $df2)",  Fstat)
    Printf.@printf("%-49s%-16s= %11.4f\n", "", "Prob > F",      pF)
    Printf.@printf("%-49s%-16s= %11.4f\n", "", "R-squared",     r2)
    println()

    # Coefficient table (slopes first, _cons last)
    order = vcat(collect(slope), 1)
    lvl   = round(Int, 100 * level)
    coef_df = DataFrames.DataFrame(
        Variable    = cn[order],
        Coefficient = β[order],
        StdErr      = se[order],
        t           = t_stat[order],
        p           = pvals[order],
        CI_low      = ci_lo[order],
        CI_high     = ci_hi[order],
    )
    _pt_compat(coef_df;
        header = (["",          "",            "Linearized", "",  "",      "",                "" ],
                  [string(ys),  "Coefficient", "std. err.",  "t", "P>|t|",
                   "[$(lvl)% CI low]", "[$(lvl)% CI high]"]),
        formatters = vcat(
            PrettyTables.ft_printf("%.7f", [2, 3, 6, 7]),
            PrettyTables.ft_printf("%.2f", [4]),
            PrettyTables.ft_printf("%.3f", [5]),
        ),
        alignment  = [:l, :r, :r, :r, :r, :r, :r],
    )

    return (; β, V, se, t=t_stat, p=pvals, ci_lo, ci_hi,
              coefnames=cn, n_obs=n, n_strata=n_str, n_psu,
              popsize=W_tot, df=dfree,
              F=Fstat, df1=q, df2, pF, r2)
end

"""
    regress_cluster(df, y, xs; cluster, weight=nothing, level=0.95)

Stata-style `regress y xs [pweight=w], vce(cluster id)` — weighted OLS
with one-way cluster-robust standard errors. Uses Stata's hc1-flavoured
adjustment `(M/(M−1)) · (N−1)/(N−k)` on the meat matrix, t-tests on
`M − 1` degrees of freedom, model F distributed `F(q, M−1)`, and the
familiar "(Std. err. adjusted for M clusters in <id>)" banner.

`cluster` is the cluster variable (Symbol); `weight=nothing` runs plain
OLS, otherwise treats the weights as pweights. Root MSE uses pweights
normalized to sum to N.

Example:

    df_nh.uniqpsu = 2 .* df_nh.strata .+ df_nh.psu
    regress_cluster(df_nh, :hgb, [:age, :female];
                    cluster=:uniqpsu, weight=:finalwgt)
"""
function regress_cluster(df, y, xs::AbstractVector; cluster::Symbol,
                         weight::Union{Symbol,Nothing}=nothing,
                         level::Float64=0.95)
    ys     = Symbol(y)
    xsv    = [Symbol(v) for v in xs]
    needed = unique(vcat(ys, xsv, cluster))
    weight !== nothing && push!(needed, weight)
    d = DataFrames.dropmissing(df, needed)
    Y = Float64.(_rawval.(d[!, ys]))
    Xcols = [Float64.(_rawval.(d[!, v])) for v in xsv]
    X  = hcat(ones(length(Y)), Xcols...)
    c  = _rawval.(d[!, cluster])
    w  = weight === nothing ? ones(length(Y)) :
         Float64.(_rawval.(d[!, weight]))
    cn = vcat("_cons", string.(xsv))

    n = length(Y); k = size(X, 2); q = k - 1

    XW = X .* w
    A  = XW' * X
    β  = A \ (XW' * Y)
    e  = Y .- X * β
    U  = XW .* e                          # scores uᵢ = wᵢ xᵢ eᵢ

    clusters = unique(c)
    M    = length(clusters)
    meat = zeros(k, k)
    for cl in clusters
        sel = c .== cl
        s   = sum(U[sel, :]; dims=1)       # 1 × k
        meat .+= s' * s
    end
    adj   = (M / (M - 1)) * ((n - 1) / (n - k))
    A_inv = LinearAlgebra.inv(A)
    V     = adj .* (A_inv * meat * A_inv)
    se    = sqrt.(max.(LinearAlgebra.diag(V), 0.0))

    dfree  = M - 1
    t_stat = β ./ se
    tcrit  = Distributions.quantile(Distributions.TDist(dfree), 1 - (1-level)/2)
    pvals  = 2 .* (1 .- Distributions.cdf.(Distributions.TDist(dfree), abs.(t_stat)))
    ci_lo  = β .- tcrit .* se
    ci_hi  = β .+ tcrit .* se

    slope = 2:k
    Wstat = β[slope]' * (V[slope, slope] \ β[slope])
    Fstat = Wstat / q
    pF    = 1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.FDist(q, dfree), Fstat)

    # Weighted R² (sums weighted by w)
    ybar_w = sum(w .* Y) / sum(w)
    rss_w  = sum(w .* e.^2)
    tss_w  = sum(w .* (Y .- ybar_w).^2)
    r2     = 1 - rss_w / tss_w

    # Root MSE: normalize pweights to sum to N (Stata convention for pweights).
    w_norm = w .* (n / sum(w))
    rmse   = sqrt(sum(w_norm .* e.^2) / (n - k))

    _fmtn(x) = replace(string(x), r"(\d)(?=(\d{3})+$)" => s"\1,")

    Printf.@printf("%-48s%-18s= %10s\n",  "Linear regression", "Number of obs", _fmtn(n))
    Printf.@printf("%-48s%-18s= %10.2f\n", "", "F($q, $dfree)",  Fstat)
    Printf.@printf("%-48s%-18s= %10.4f\n", "", "Prob > F",       pF)
    Printf.@printf("%-48s%-18s= %10.4f\n", "", "R-squared",      r2)
    Printf.@printf("%-48s%-18s= %10.4f\n", "", "Root MSE",       rmse)
    println()
    Printf.@printf("%78s\n", "(Std. err. adjusted for $M clusters in $cluster)")

    order  = vcat(collect(slope), 1)
    lvl    = round(Int, 100 * level)
    coef_df = DataFrames.DataFrame(
        Variable    = cn[order],
        Coefficient = β[order],
        StdErr      = se[order],
        t           = t_stat[order],
        p           = pvals[order],
        CI_low      = ci_lo[order],
        CI_high     = ci_hi[order],
    )
    _pt_compat(coef_df;
        header = (["",          "",            "Robust",     "",  "",      "",                "" ],
                  [string(ys),  "Coefficient", "std. err.",  "t", "P>|t|",
                   "[$(lvl)% CI low]", "[$(lvl)% CI high]"]),
        formatters = vcat(
            PrettyTables.ft_printf("%.7f", [2, 3, 6, 7]),
            PrettyTables.ft_printf("%.2f", [4]),
            PrettyTables.ft_printf("%.3f", [5]),
        ),
        alignment = [:l, :r, :r, :r, :r, :r, :r],
    )
    return (; β, V, se, t=t_stat, p=pvals, ci_lo, ci_hi, coefnames=cn,
              n_obs=n, M, df=dfree, F=Fstat, df1=q, df2=dfree, pF, r2, rmse)
end

"""
    estat_hettest(model, df; vars=nothing, iid=false, mtest=false)

Breusch-Pagan / Cook-Weisberg test for heteroskedasticity.
Replicates Stata's `estat hettest [varlist] [, iid] [, mtest]`.

- No `vars`:  test against fitted values (1 df).
- With `vars`: test against the listed variables (joint + individual).
- `iid=true`:  uses the NR^2 form (regress u^2/s^2 on z; LM = n*R^2)
               matching Stata's `estat hettest, iid`.
- `iid=false` (default): uses the score form (Koenker, 1981) which is
               robust to non-normal errors — this is Stata's default.
- `mtest=true`: also reports Bonferroni and Sidak adjusted p-values
               for each variable individually.
"""
function estat_hettest(model, df;
                       vars::Union{Nothing, Vector{Symbol}} = nothing,
                       iid::Bool = false,
                       mtest::Bool = false)
    beta = StatsBase.coef(model)
    nm   = StatsBase.coefnames(model)
    n    = Int(StatsBase.nobs(model))

    # Get fitted values and residuals
    # Build yhat from coefficients and data
    yhat = zeros(n)
    uhat = zeros(n)

    # Use dropmissing on needed columns
    needed = Symbol[]
    for name in nm
        name == "(Intercept)" && continue
        s = Symbol(strip(split(name, ":")[1]))
        hasproperty(df, s) && push!(needed, s)
    end
    resp = Symbol(split(string(FixedEffectModels.formula(model).lhs), "(")[end] |>
                  s -> replace(s, ")" => ""))
    push!(needed, resp)
    unique!(needed)
    dfc = dropmissing(df, needed)

    # Predict using FixedEffectModels
    yhat = FixedEffectModels.predict(model, dfc)
    uhat = Float64.(dfc[!, resp]) .- yhat

    sigma2 = sum(uhat.^2) / n     # MLE variance (divide by n)

    if vars === nothing
        z = hcat(ones(n), yhat)
        varnames = ["Fitted values"]
        q = 1
    else
        z = hcat(ones(n), [Float64.([_rawval(x) for x in dfc[!, v]]) for v in vars]...)
        varnames = string.(vars)
        q = length(vars)
    end

    # Helper: compute BP chi2 for given dep variable and regressors
    function _bp_chi2(dep, z, is_iid)
        b = z \ dep
        fitted = z * b
        if is_iid
            # Koenker (iid) form: n * R^2 of e^2 on z
            ss_tot = sum((dep .- mean(dep)).^2)
            ss_res = sum((dep .- fitted).^2)
            return ss_tot > 0 ? n * (1 - ss_res / ss_tot) : 0.0
        else
            # Normal (default) form: h = e^2/sigma^2, regress h on z, chi2 = ESS/2
            # Equivalently: ESS of e^2 on z, divided by 2*sigma^4
            ess = sum((fitted .- mean(dep)).^2)
            return ess / (2 * sigma2^2)
        end
    end

    chi2 = _bp_chi2(uhat.^2, z, iid)
    pval = 1 - cdf(Chisq(q), chi2)

    # Print Stata-style output
    form = iid ? "i.i.d." : "Normal"
    if mtest && vars !== nothing && length(vars) > 1
        # mtest format: individual + simultaneous table
        println("\nBreusch-Pagan / Cook-Weisberg test for heteroskedasticity")
        @printf("Assumption: %s error terms\n", form)
        println("H0: Constant variance\n")
        println("-"^38)
        @printf("    Variable |      chi2   df        p\n")
        println("-"^13, "+", "-"^24)

        dep_sq = uhat.^2
        for v in vars
            zj = hcat(ones(n), Float64.([_rawval(x) for x in dfc[!, v]]))
            chi2_j = _bp_chi2(dep_sq, zj, iid)
            p_j = 1 - cdf(Chisq(1), chi2_j)
            @printf("%12s | %9.2f    1   %.4f*\n", v, chi2_j, p_j)
        end
        println("-"^13, "+", "-"^24)
        @printf("Simultaneous | %9.2f    %d   %.4f\n", chi2, q, pval)
        println("-"^38)
        println("* Unadjusted p-values")
    else
        # Standard format: single test
        var_label = vars === nothing ? "Fitted values of $(resp)" : join(varnames, ", ")
        println("\nBreusch-Pagan / Cook-Weisberg test for heteroskedasticity")
        @printf("Assumption: %s error terms\n", form)
        println("Variable: $(var_label)")
        println("\nH0: Constant variance\n")
        @printf("    chi2(%d) = %6.2f\n", q, chi2)
        @printf("Prob > chi2 = %.4f\n", pval)
    end

    return (; chi2, df = q, p = pval)
end
```

drop uhat
=#
# Breusch–Pagan test of heteroskedasticity (regress uhat² on regressors)
df5.uhat2 = df5.uhat.^2
m_bp5 = FixedEffectModels.reg(df5, @formula(uhat2 ~ x2 + x3))
LM = nrow(df5) * StatsBase.r2(m_bp5)

```{julia}
#=
* Test heteroskedasticity depending on x2, x3, and x2 and x3
estat hettest x2 x3, mtest
=#
# estat hettest x2 x3, mtest  (individual + joint tests with Bonferroni/Sidak corrections)
p_individual = Float64[]
for v in (:x2, :x3)
    m = FixedEffectModels.reg(df5, term(:uhat2) ~ term(v))
    LM = nrow(df5) * StatsBase.r2(m)
    p = 1 - cdf(Chisq(1), LM)
    push!(p_individual, p)
    @printf("BP test on %s only: LM(1) = %.4f, p = %.4f\n", v, LM, p)
end
# Multiple-testing corrections (mtest)
ntests = length(p_individual)
for (i, (vname, p)) in enumerate(zip(["x2", "x3"], p_individual))
    p_bonf = min(p * ntests, 1.0)
    p_sidak = 1 - (1 - p)^ntests
    @printf("  %s: Bonferroni p = %.4f, Šidák p = %.4f\n", vname, p_bonf, p_sidak)
end
# Joint test
m_joint = FixedEffectModels.reg(df5, @formula(uhat2 ~ x2 + x3))
LM_joint = nrow(df5) * StatsBase.r2(m_joint)
@printf("BP joint test on x2 x3: LM(2) = %.4f, p = %.4f\n",
        LM_joint, 1 - cdf(Chisq(2), LM_joint))
```

### 5.3.4 FGLS estimation

```{julia}
#=
clear all
* Generated data for heteroskedasticity example
set seed 10101
quietly set obs 500
generate double x2 = 5*rnormal(0)
generate double x3 = 5*rnormal(0)
generate double e  = 5*rnormal(0)
generate double u  = sqrt(exp(-1+0.2*x2))*e
generate double y  = 1 + 1*x2 + 1*x3 + u
export delimited using "musr/5_3_1.csv", replace

* FGLS: First step get estimate of skedasticity function
quietly regress y x2 x3                  // get bols
predict double uhat, resid
generate double uhatsq = uhat^2          // get squared residual 
generate double one = 1 
* NLS of uhatsq on exp(z'a)                      
capture nl (uhatsq = exp({xb: x2 one})), nolog   
=#
# FGLS step 1: estimate skedasticity function via NLS:  σ²(x) = exp(α0 + α1·x2)
function neg_lik(α, x, y)
    pred = exp.(α[1] .+ α[2] .* x)
    sum((y .- pred).^2)
end
res_α = optimize(α -> neg_lik(α, df5.x2, df5.uhat2), [0.0, 0.0])
α_hat = Optim.minimizer(res_α)
df5.varu = exp.(α_hat[1] .+ α_hat[2] .* df5.x2)
@printf("α̂ = (%.4f, %.4f)\n", α_hat[1], α_hat[2])
```

fgls5 = FixedEffectModels.reg(df5, @formula(y ~ x2 + x3), weights = :w_fgls)

```{julia}
# SUR estimation (FGLS) — sureg (ldrugexp ...) (ltotothr ...), corr
# Step 1: equation-by-equation OLS to get Σ̂; Step 2: FGLS using Σ⁻¹ ⊗ I_N
sur_data = dropmissing(df_sur, [:ldrugexp, :ltotothr, :age, :age2, :educyr, :actlim, :totchr, :medicaid, :private])
Ns = nrow(sur_data)

# Design matrices (equation-specific regressors)
X1 = hcat(ones(Ns), sur_data.age, sur_data.age2, sur_data.actlim,
          sur_data.totchr, sur_data.medicaid, sur_data.private)
X2 = hcat(ones(Ns), sur_data.age, sur_data.age2, sur_data.educyr,
          sur_data.actlim, sur_data.totchr, sur_data.private)
Y1 = Float64.(sur_data.ldrugexp)
Y2 = Float64.(sur_data.ltotothr)
cn1 = ["_cons", "age", "age2", "actlim", "totchr", "medicaid", "private"]
cn2 = ["_cons", "age", "age2", "educyr", "actlim", "totchr", "private"]

# Step 1: OLS residuals
β1_ols = X1 \ Y1;  e1 = Y1 - X1 * β1_ols
β2_ols = X2 \ Y2;  e2 = Y2 - X2 * β2_ols
Σ̂ = [e1'e1 e1'e2; e2'e1 e2'e2] ./ Ns

# Step 2: FGLS (SUR)
Σinv = LinearAlgebra.inv(Σ̂)
# Block structure: X = blockdiag(X1, X2), W = Σ⁻¹ ⊗ I_N
XWX = Σinv[1,1]*(X1'X1) + zeros(size(X1,2), size(X2,2))
XWX = [Σinv[1,1]*(X1'X1)  Σinv[1,2]*(X1'X2);
       Σinv[2,1]*(X2'X1)  Σinv[2,2]*(X2'X2)]
XWY = [Σinv[1,1]*(X1'Y1) + Σinv[1,2]*(X1'Y2);
       Σinv[2,1]*(X2'Y1) + Σinv[2,2]*(X2'Y2)]
β_sur = XWX \ XWY
V_sur = LinearAlgebra.inv(XWX)
se_sur = sqrt.(max.(LinearAlgebra.diag(V_sur), 0.0))

k1 = size(X1, 2); k2 = size(X2, 2)
println("=== SUR (FGLS) Equation 1: ldrugexp ===")
_pt_compat(
    DataFrame(variable=cn1, Coef=β_sur[1:k1], SE=se_sur[1:k1],
              z=β_sur[1:k1]./se_sur[1:k1]);
    formatters=PrettyTables.ft_printf("%.6f", 2:4))
println("\n=== SUR (FGLS) Equation 2: ltotothr ===")
_pt_compat(
    DataFrame(variable=cn2, Coef=β_sur[k1+1:end], SE=se_sur[k1+1:end],
              z=β_sur[k1+1:end]./se_sur[k1+1:end]);
    formatters=PrettyTables.ft_printf("%.6f", 2:4))

# Cross-equation residual correlation (corr option)
rho = Σ̂[1,2] / sqrt(Σ̂[1,1] * Σ̂[2,2])
@printf("\nCorrelation matrix of residuals:\n  ldrugexp  ltotothr\n  1.0000    %.4f\n  %.4f    1.0000\n", rho, rho)
@printf("Breusch-Pagan test of independence: chi2(1) = %.3f, Pr = %.4f\n",
        Ns * rho^2, 1 - cdf(Chisq(1), Ns * rho^2))

# Save OLS-based models for later use (bootstrap, testparm)
eq1 = FixedEffectModels.reg(sur_data, @formula(ldrugexp ~ age + age2 + actlim + totchr + medicaid + private))
eq2 = FixedEffectModels.reg(sur_data, @formula(ltotothr ~ age + age2 + educyr + actlim + totchr + private))
```

      :ldrugexp => [:age, :age2, :actlim, :totchr, :medicaid, :private],

### 5.4.4 Robust standard errors

```{julia}
#=
* Bootstrap to get heteroskedasticity-robust SEs for SUR estimator 
bootstrap, reps(400) seed(10101) nodots: sureg        ///
  (ldrugexp age age2 actlim totchr medicaid private)  ///
  (ltotothr age age2 educyr actlim totchr private) 
=#
# Bootstrap to obtain SEs for the two SUR equations (B = 400)
Random.seed!(10101)
B = 400
β1_boot = Vector{Vector{Float64}}(undef, B)
β2_boot = Vector{Vector{Float64}}(undef, B)
for b in 1:B
    idx = sample(1:nrow(sur_data), nrow(sur_data); replace = true)
    sub = sur_data[idx, :]
    m1 = FixedEffectModels.reg(sub, @formula(ldrugexp ~ age + age2 + actlim + totchr + medicaid + private))
    m2 = FixedEffectModels.reg(sub, @formula(ltotothr ~ age + age2 + educyr + actlim + totchr + private))
    β1_boot[b] = StatsBase.coef(m1)
    β2_boot[b] = StatsBase.coef(m2)
end
β1_mat = reduce(hcat, β1_boot)'
β2_mat = reduce(hcat, β2_boot)'
println("Eq1 bootstrap SEs: ", round.(std(β1_mat, dims = 1), digits = 4))
println("Eq2 bootstrap SEs: ", round.(std(β2_mat, dims = 1), digits = 4))
```

### 5.4.5 Testing cross-equation constraints

```{julia}
#=
* Test of variables in both equations
quietly sureg (ldrugexp age age2 actlim totchr medicaid private) ///
   (ltotothr age age2 educyr actlim totchr private)
test age age2
=#
# Joint Wald test of age and age2 in equation 1
nm = StatsBase.coefnames(eq1)
idx = [findfirst(==(n), nm) for n in ("age", "age2")]
βt  = StatsBase.coef(eq1)[idx]; Vt = StatsBase.vcov(eq1)[idx, idx]
W = try
    βt' * LinearAlgebra.inv(Vt) * βt
catch
    NaN
end
@printf("W(2) = %.4f, p = %.4f\n", W, 1 - cdf(Chisq(2), W))
```

```{julia}
#=
* Test of variables in just the first equation
test [ldrugexp]age [ldrugexp]age2
=#
# Test of age and age2 in equation 1 only (same as above)
println("Same Wald test on equation 1; see above.")
```

```{julia}
#=
* Test of a restriction across the two equations
test [ldrugexp]private = [ltotothr]private
=#
# Cross-equation restriction:  β_private (eq1) = β_private (eq2)
# Test using the bootstrap distribution
β1_priv = β1_mat[:, findfirst(==("private"), StatsBase.coefnames(eq1))]
β2_priv = β2_mat[:, findfirst(==("private"), StatsBase.coefnames(eq2))]
diff_b  = β1_priv .- β2_priv
@printf("mean(diff) = %.4f  bootstrap SE = %.4f  z = %.3f\n",
        mean(diff_b), std(diff_b), mean(diff_b) / std(diff_b))
```

```{julia}
# sureg (ldrugexp age age2 actlim totchr medicaid private) ///
#       (ltotothr age age2 educyr actlim totchr private)
# test age age2
#
# Joint test of age and age2 across BOTH equations (4 restrictions).
# Uses the bootstrap draws computed earlier (β1_mat, β2_mat) to estimate the
# joint covariance — equation-by-equation OLS vcov misses the cross-equation
# correlation that Stata's sureg accounts for via FGLS.
i1 = [findfirst(==(n), StatsBase.coefnames(eq1)) for n in ("age", "age2")]
i2 = [findfirst(==(n), StatsBase.coefnames(eq2)) for n in ("age", "age2")]

β_joint = vcat(StatsBase.coef(eq1)[i1], StatsBase.coef(eq2)[i2])
B_joint = hcat(β1_mat[:, i1], β2_mat[:, i2])      # B × 4 bootstrap draws
V_joint = Statistics.cov(B_joint)

W = β_joint' * (V_joint \ β_joint)
q = length(β_joint)
p = 1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Chisq(q), W)
Printf.@printf("Joint Wald test: H0 : age = age2 = 0 in both equations\n")
Printf.@printf("  chi2(%d) = %.4f   p = %.4f\n", q, W, p)
```

### 5.4.6 Imposing cross-equation constraints

```{julia}
#=
* Specify a restriction across the two equations
constraint 1 [ldrugexp]private = [ltotothr]private
=#
# constraint 1 [ldrugexp]private = [ltotothr]private
# sureg (ldrugexp age age2 actlim totchr medicaid private) ///
#       (ltotothr age age2 educyr actlim totchr private), constraints(1)
#
# Strategy: stack the two equations into a single regression where `private`
# appears as ONE shared regressor (its coefficient is the constrained value).
# All other regressors are "padded" with zeros in the other equation's block.
# A first OLS pass on the stacked system gives a consistent restricted
# estimate; a second FGLS pass uses Σ̂ from those residuals for efficiency,
# matching what Stata's `sureg ... , constraints()` does.

N = DataFrames.nrow(sur_data)
pad1(v) = vcat(Float64.(v), zeros(N))
pad2(v) = vcat(zeros(N), Float64.(v))

Y  = vcat(Float64.(sur_data.ldrugexp), Float64.(sur_data.ltotothr))
X  = hcat(
    pad1(ones(N)),              # ldrugexp: intercept
    pad1(sur_data.age),
    pad1(sur_data.age2),
    pad1(sur_data.actlim),
    pad1(sur_data.totchr),
    pad1(sur_data.medicaid),
    pad2(ones(N)),              # ltotothr: intercept
    pad2(sur_data.age),
    pad2(sur_data.age2),
    pad2(sur_data.educyr),
    pad2(sur_data.actlim),
    pad2(sur_data.totchr),
    vcat(Float64.(sur_data.private), Float64.(sur_data.private))   # SHARED
)
cnames = ["eq1:_cons", "eq1:age", "eq1:age2", "eq1:actlim", "eq1:totchr", "eq1:medicaid",
          "eq2:_cons", "eq2:age", "eq2:age2", "eq2:educyr", "eq2:actlim", "eq2:totchr",
          "private (shared)"]
k = size(X, 2)

# --- First pass: OLS on the stacked system (restricted) ---
β_ols = X \ Y
e     = reshape(Y - X*β_ols, N, 2)            # per-observation residuals for the 2 equations

# --- Second pass: FGLS using Σ̂ from first-pass residuals ---
Σ̂    = (e' * e) / N                            # 2×2 cross-equation covariance
Σinv = LinearAlgebra.inv(Σ̂)
# Weight matrix W = Σ⁻¹ ⊗ I_N: efficient SUR moments are  X' W Y  and  X' W X
W_lhs = Σinv[1,1]*(X[1:N,     :]'X[1:N,     :]) +
        Σinv[2,2]*(X[N+1:end, :]'X[N+1:end, :]) +
        Σinv[1,2]*(X[1:N,     :]'X[N+1:end, :]) +
        Σinv[2,1]*(X[N+1:end, :]'X[1:N,     :])
W_rhs = Σinv[1,1]*(X[1:N,     :]'Y[1:N])      +
        Σinv[2,2]*(X[N+1:end, :]'Y[N+1:end]) +
        Σinv[1,2]*(X[1:N,     :]'Y[N+1:end]) +
        Σinv[2,1]*(X[N+1:end, :]'Y[1:N])
β_fgls = W_lhs \ W_rhs
V_fgls = LinearAlgebra.inv(W_lhs)              # joint FGLS vcov
se     = sqrt.(max.(LinearAlgebra.diag(V_fgls), 0.0))
z      = β_fgls ./ se
pval   = 2 .* (1 .- Distributions.cdf.(Distributions.Normal(), abs.(z)))

println("FGLS (SUR) with cross-equation constraint  [ldrugexp]private = [ltotothr]private")
println("Residual cov matrix Σ̂ =")
_pt_compat(Σ̂; header=["ldrugexp","ltotothr"], row_labels=["ldrugexp","ltotothr"])
println("\nCoefficients:")
_pt_compat(
    DataFrames.DataFrame(variable=cnames, estimate=β_fgls, stderr=se, z=z, p=pval);
    formatters = PrettyTables.ft_printf("%.6f", 2:5))
```

```{julia}
#=
* Estimate subject to the cross-equation constraint
sureg (ldrugexp age age2 actlim totchr medicaid private)        ///
  (ltotothr age age2 educyr actlim totchr private), constraints(1)
=#
#* Specify a restriction across the two equations
#constraint 1 [ldrugexp]private = [ltotothr]private

#* Estimate subject to the cross-equation constraint
#sureg (ldrugexp age age2 actlim totchr medicaid private)        ///
#  (ltotothr age age2 educyr actlim totchr private), constraints(1)
sureg(df_sur,
      :ldrugexp => [:age, :age2, :actlim, :totchr, :medicaid, :private],
      :ltotothr => [:age, :age2, :educyr, :actlim, :totchr, :private];
      constraints = ["[ldrugexp]private = [ltotothr]private"])
```

## 5.5 Survey data: Weighting, clustering, and stratification

### 5.5.1 Survey design

```{julia}
#=
* Data from http://www.stata-press.com/data/r10/nhanes2.dta

* Survey data example: NHANES II data
clear all
use musr/mus05nhanes2.dta
quietly keep if age >= 21 & age <= 65
describe sampl finalwgt strata psu
summarize sampl finalwgt strata psu
=#
# NHANES II data
df_nh = DataFrame(ReadStatTables.readstat("musr/mus05nhanes2.dta"))
df_nh = filter(r -> 21 <= r.age <= 65, df_nh)
@printf("N = %d\n", nrow(df_nh))
DataFrames.describe(df_nh[:, [:sampl, :finalwgt, :strata, :psu]])
```


```{julia}
#=
* Declare survey design
svyset psu [pweight=finalwgt], strata(strata)
=#
summarize_stata(df_nh[:, [:sampl, :finalwgt, :strata, :psu]])
```

```{julia}
#=
* Describe the survey design
svydescribe
=#
# Stata's svyset is descriptive — record the design columns for later use
println("Survey design: PSU = :psu, strata = :strata, weight = :finalwgt")
```

```{julia}
# Describe the survey design (counts of strata and PSUs)
@printf("Number of strata = %d\n", length(unique(df_nh.strata)))
@printf("Number of PSUs   = %d\n",
        length(unique(zip(df_nh.strata, df_nh.psu) |> collect)))
```

### 5.5.2 Survey mean estimation

```{julia}
#=
* Estimate the population mean using svy:
svy: mean hgb
=#
# Population mean of hgb using sampling weights
let df = dropmissing(df_nh[:, [:hgb, :finalwgt]])
    @printf("Weighted mean of hgb = %.4f\n",
            sum(df.hgb .* df.finalwgt) / sum(df.finalwgt))
end
```

```{julia}
#=
* Estimate the population mean using no weights and no cluster
mean hgb
=#
# Unweighted mean of hgb
@printf("Unweighted mean of hgb = %.4f\n",
        mean(skipmissing(df_nh.hgb)))
```


```{julia}
#* Estimate the population mean using svy:
#svy: mean hgb
svy_mean(df_nh, :hgb; stratum=:strata, psu=:psu, weight=:finalwgt);
```

```{julia}
#* Estimate the population mean using no weights and no cluster
#mean hgb
mean_stata(df_nh, :hgb);
```

### 5.5.3 Survey linear regression

```{julia}
#=
* Regression using svy:
svy: regress hgb age female
=#
# Regression with weights (no cluster correction)
m_svy = FixedEffectModels.reg(df_nh, @formula(hgb ~ age + female),
            weights = :finalwgt)
```

```{julia}
#=
* Regression using weights and cluster on PSU
generate uniqpsu = 2*strata + psu  // make unique identifier for each psu
regress hgb age female [pweight=finalwgt], vce(cluster uniqpsu)
=#
# Regression with weights + clustering on unique PSU = 2·strata + psu
df_nh.uniqpsu = 2 .* df_nh.strata .+ df_nh.psu
reg(df_nh, @formula(hgb ~ age + female),
    weights = :finalwgt, Vcov.cluster(:uniqpsu))
```

```{julia}
#=
* Regression using no weights and no cluster
regress hgb age female
=#
# Regression with no weights, no cluster
reg(df_nh, @formula(hgb ~ age + female))
```


```{julia}
#* Regression using svy:
#svy: regress hgb age female
svy_regress(df_nh, :hgb, [:age, :female];
            stratum=:strata, psu=:psu, weight=:finalwgt);
```


```{julia}
#* Regression using weights and cluster on PSU
#generate uniqpsu = 2*strata + psu  // make unique identifier for each psu
#regress hgb age female [pweight=finalwgt], vce(cluster uniqpsu)
df_nh.uniqpsu = 2 .* df_nh.strata .+ df_nh.psu
regress_cluster(df_nh, :hgb, [:age, :female];
                cluster=:uniqpsu, weight=:finalwgt);
```

```{julia}
#* Regression using no weights and no cluster
#regress hgb age female
regress_stata(df_nh, :hgb, [:age, :female]);
```
